name: mesh stress — Stanford 3D Scanning Repository, full resolution
comment: The mesh counterpart of the lidar ladder. Source: graphics.stanford.edu/data/3Dscanrep. NONE of these models ship per-vertex colour ('XYZ RGB' is the scanner manufacturer, not colour data) - the colours here are SYNTHESIZED at conversion from the area-weighted vertex normal (n*0.5+0.5), so what you are looking at is direction, not measurement. Bunny and Armadillo do carry a real per-vertex/per-face 'intensity' channel that could be used instead. The models arrive at wildly different native scales - bunny is 0.156 units across, armadillo is 151 - so each carries a uniform scale in its xform that brings it to about 2 m, spaced 3 m apart. xform is column-major, scale on the diagonal, translation in slots 12-14. Rungs beyond dragon are in 'ladder': they need the halfedge flattening before they can exist at all - see the comment there.

ladder.comment: NOT CONVERTED. Measured on the three above, a kernel Mesh costs ~3.7 KB per vertex to BUILD and the .pb lands at ~520 B per vertex, both linear. Asian Dragon (3,609,600 v) therefore needs ~12.6 GB to convert and produces a ~1.8 GB .pb; Thai Statue (4,999,996 v) needs ~17.5 GB and ~2.5 GB. Neither fits on this machine, and neither would load in a 4 GB wasm32 address space. They become reachable when the halfedge stops being a HashMap per vertex.
